steps.title: Python environment and AWS context

blocks.text: Prepare dependencies and confirm the AWS context before the supplied automation script runs.
An application’s virtual environment isolates its interpreter context and installed Python packages.
Create the environment with python -m venv ENV_DIR. Activate it with your platform’s command; on Unix, for example, use source ENV_DIR/bin/activate.
Inside the environment, install supplied requirements with python -m pip install -r requirements.txt. Inspect packages with python -m pip list, then use that interpreter for the supplied script.
Before AWS automation runs, confirm the approved AWS profile and Region through the supplied credential configuration.

steps.title: Complete structured CLI inventory

blocks.text: An inventory needs complete results from the approved account and Region.
For supported commands, AWS CLI follows service-side pagination automatically unless automatic pagination is disabled.
For structured inventory, specify --profile, --region and --output json. Leave out --no-paginate when you need the full listing.
--page-size adjusts service-call page size, not total output count. --max-items bounds output; retain a returned NextToken and use --starting-token to collect the remainder manually.

Keep explicit profile, Region and JSON output on the supplied supported inventory command. A full listing keeps automatic pagination enabled. A deliberately bounded --max-items listing retains NextToken for --starting-token continuation. Preserve continuation evidence with the inventory.
Smaller service pages do not imply fewer total results. --page-size and --max-items control different limits; manual continuation must not discard NextToken.

blocks.title: Complete structured CLI inventory
blocks.alt_text: Automatic collection follows requests and responses until no results remain. Bounded --max-items collection resumes NextToken with --starting-token, keeping the same explicit profile and Region. --page-size changes service-call size, not total output.

steps.title: An actionable restart runbook

blocks.text: The receiving operator needs observable results, not the author’s memory.
A runbook records procedures for a known operational outcome and should be usable by the operator doing the task.
Make preconditions, action order and expected results explicit so the operator checks execution instead of inferring it.
Include failure handling and escalation: state when routine work stops and identify who takes over.

In the orders restart record, compare preconditions with the approved task before the restart. Check each expected result before advancing, including the supplied health result. Keep the stop condition and escalation recipient visible; do not invent a recovery action.
An action list alone is insufficient. Preconditions, expected results and failure/escalation instructions make the task checkable.

steps.title: Read Pod and container evidence

blocks.text: A Running Pod still needs container and event evidence.
A Pod groups containers sharing networking and storage. Its lifecycle is distinct from a controller that may replace it.
Pod phases include Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed and Unknown. A phase alone does not fully diagnose container health.
Inspect status with kubectl get pod NAME, events with kubectl describe pod NAME, and the intended container’s output with kubectl logs NAME -c CONTAINER.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Read Pod and container evidence

blocks.text: Read the supplied Pod’s status, described events and named container’s logs together. For Pending, use scheduling-event evidence rather than guessing a correction. For Running, inspect runtime events and output. Another container’s logs do not establish the named container’s condition.
Running is a lifecycle phase, not a complete health diagnosis. Keep status, events and the intended container’s output together.

steps.title: Recoverable S3 versions

blocks.text: Choose the recovery method for the actual overwrite or simple-deletion case.
S3 versioning retains multiple object versions, including versions displaced by an overwrite.
In a versioning-enabled bucket, a simple delete ordinarily adds a delete marker rather than removing earlier versions. Deleting a specified version removes it permanently.
For an overwrite, copy the selected prior version to the same key, creating a new current version. Undo a simple deletion by removing its delete marker to expose the preceding version.
Check noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window so needed recoverable versions remain available.

blocks.title: Illustrative schematic histories: releases/orders.zip

nodes.label: Simple deletion: delete marker above preceding version
Versioning enabled; inspect noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window
Deleting a specified version is permanent.

Overwrite: selected prior version → copy selected prior version → Copy to releases/orders.zip; Copy to releases/orders.zip → creates → New current version; Simple deletion: delete marker above preceding version → undo simple deletion → Remove marker; Remove marker → exposes → Preceding version exposed; Versioning enabled; inspect noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window → overwrite recovery window → Overwrite: selected prior version; Versioning enabled; inspect noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window → simple-deletion recovery window → Simple deletion: delete marker above preceding version; Versioning enabled; inspect noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window → specified-version deletion is distinct → Deleting a specified version is permanent.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Recoverable S3 versions

blocks.text: For overwritten releases/orders.zip, copy the required prior version to the same key to create a new current version. For a separate simple deletion, remove the delete marker to expose the preceding version. Check lifecycle expiration against the required recovery window; do not permanently delete a needed specified version.
A simple delete ordinarily creates a marker; a specified-version deletion is permanent. Versioning alone does not guarantee indefinite retention under lifecycle rules.

steps.title: Publish and consume exact image content

blocks.text: Keep the publication reference distinct from the exact-content retrieval reference.
ECR repositories store container images; assigned image digests identify the content.
Authenticate Docker by piping aws ecr get-login-password --region REGION to docker login --username AWS --password-stdin REGISTRY.
Tag the already-built image as REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG, then docker push that reference.
Retrieve exact content with docker pull REGISTRY/REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST. Verify access separately with the approved publisher and consumer identities.

Supplied orders output: revision rev-42 → upload same supplied file → Immutable upload record: workflow run, revision-based artifact name, upload SHA256; Immutable upload record: workflow run, revision-based artifact name, upload SHA256 → Upload/download digest check → Download integrity result: upload SHA256 matches; Download integrity result: upload SHA256 matches → Extracted-file provenance verification → Verified extracted-file attestation: artifact digest, source repository, revision rev-42, build workflow/run; Verified extracted-file attestation: artifact digest, source repository, revision rev-42, build workflow/run → verified revision/workflow linked to upload record → Immutable upload record: workflow run, revision-based artifact name, upload SHA256; Supplied orders output: revision rev-42 → same revision rev-42 → Verified extracted-file attestation: artifact digest, source repository, revision rev-42, build workflow/run

steps.title: The verification sequence: Trace an immutable build artifact

blocks.text: For the supplied output file, set id-token: write, contents: read and attestations: write. Use actions/attest@v4 with subject-path set to that file, then actions/upload-artifact@v4 with path set to it and the supplied revision-based name. Retain the run, artifact name and upload SHA256 digest as the immutable content reference; v4 artifacts are immutable.

Use actions/download-artifact: it checks the upload SHA256 digest and warns on mismatch. Verify the extracted output’s provenance with gh attestation verify PATH/TO/YOUR/BUILD/ARTIFACT-BINARY -R ORGANIZATION_NAME/REPOSITORY_NAME --format json. Before deployment, inspect the verified attestation’s source revision and build workflow/run.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Trace an immutable build artifact

blocks.text: For the supplied orders output at rev-42, attest and upload the same file using the required permissions and revision-based name. Retain the run, name and upload digest. After download, inspect any mismatch warning and verify the extracted file’s attestation for the approved repository, revision and workflow/run.
Download integrity and provenance are different checks. A digest-mismatch warning is not a promise to block every mismatch, nor proof of the intended source revision.

steps.title: Read declaration and deployed bucket evidence

blocks.text: The requested declaration and the live deployed property need separate evidence.
In a CloudFormation template, Resources declares each resource through its logical ID, Type and Properties.
Type: AWS::S3::Bucket declares an S3 bucket. Ref on that logical ID returns the bucket name.
Change the supplied declared property and references. Validate with aws cloudformation validate-template --template-body file://TEMPLATE, then create the sandbox stack from the approved template.
Confirm deployment by inspecting stack events, outputs and the bucket’s live value for the declared property.
